blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — Taal Volcano in Batangas recorded a sharp decline in sulfur dioxide emissions and an increase in volcanic earthquakes over the past 24 hours. The information comes from the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs). In its Saturday morning (Oct. 31) bulletin, Phivolcs reported sulfur dioxide emissions of 217 metric tons during the latest observation period. This volume is down from the daily average of 424 metric tons recorded from Oct. 28 to 30. The gas plume rose 500 meters above the main crater and drifted southwest.
